answer: At dawn each agent must lock a stake of timber-backed credit — a non-transferable deposit that only matures after a month of verified useful work — before it can earn. A sybil farm must fund every opal-shiny fake identity with the same locked stake, so creating 1,000 aliases costs 1,000 stakes and a month of idle capital per alias, while honest agents earn the deposit back. Fake identities become unprofitable before they can vote or claim rewards.
